_impervious-guide-prior-sources.provenance: src/data/guides.ts at a3f7bd7a41a556d950ee4d377f844260517dd876; source list for is-artificial-turf-impervious
_impervious-guide-prior-sources.status: Prior research retained internally after the public guide was shortened; not reverified in this editorial pass.
_impervious-guide-prior-sources.limits: Original citations and checked dates are preserved as historical research, not a new legal or parcel determination. Historical search-absence statements and proposed rules are not current publication authority. In particular, current Horry permitting guidance supersedes any blanket exemption inference from the old manual.

sources.label: 21 NCAC 28B .0503(b) — NC Landscape Contractors' Licensing Board rules
sources.cite: Artificial turf workmanship standard: "Ensure that the sub-grade is compacted and shall pitch properly to drain", plus perimeter attachment, nap direction, an evenly weighted sand layer and manufacturer specifications.

sources.label: Brunswick County Stormwater Quality Management and Discharge Control Ordinance
sources.cite: Section 1.5(d) defines built-upon area with exclusions for slatted wood decks, pool water, #57 stone over geotextile and trails — artificial turf is not listed.

sources.label: Brunswick County Unified Development Ordinance
sources.cite: Impervious surface defined to include compacted earth and gravel. Full-text search of the 491-page UDO returns no occurrence of "artificial turf" or "synthetic turf". The Water Quality Protection Overlay at Sec. 4.8.7.E caps built-upon area at 25 percent of the lot.

sources.label: Town of Shallotte Unified Development Ordinance (amendments through April 2026)
sources.cite: Impervious surface at (126) covers compacted earth, gravel, concrete and asphalt; built-upon area covers "buildings, pavement, gravel roads, and recreation facilities". Neither definition has been conformed to G.S. 143-214.7D.

sources.label: Town of Sunset Beach Unified Development Ordinance
sources.cite: "Alternative materials, not subject to the definition of impervious surface, may be proposed subject to certification of a licensed and certified North Carolina professional engineer of compliance with the hydraulic conductivity standard of 1.41 inches per hour or greater. Such certification shall be in the form of a letter under seal."

sources.label: Horry County Code Sec. 17.7-16 (Stormwater Utility, Definitions)
sources.cite: "Common impervious surfaces include, but are not limited to, rooftops, sidewalks, walkways, patio areas, driveways, parking lots, storage areas, compacted gravel and soil surfaces, awnings and other fabric or plastic coverings, and other surfaces which prevent or impede the natural infiltration of stormwater runoff which existed prior to development." Artificial turf is not named.

sources.label: Horry County Code Sec. 17.7-17 (Stormwater service charge)
sources.cite: Non-single-family parcels are assigned a development intensity factor by impervious percentage — 90–100% = 0.95 down to less than 1% = 0.01 — billed per 20,000 square feet of land area.

sources.label: Horry County Stormwater Management Design Manual (January 2024)
sources.cite: Sec. 2.3: a stormwater permit is required where one-half acre or more will be disturbed, or the construction is part of a Larger Common Plan. No mention of artificial turf, synthetic turf or synthetic grass appears in its 134 pages. Note: horrycountysc.gov was unreachable on the check date, so the document was read from the Internet Archive capture of this URL dated 2026-04-15.

sources.label: Myrtle Beach Zoning Code, Appendix A Sec. 203
sources.cite: "Impervious Surface: Any material that prevents, impedes, or slows infiltration or absorption of storm and surface water directly into the ground at the rate of absorption of vegetations-bearing soils." Impervious lot coverage expressly counts "stone, shell or gravel surfacing".

sources.label: Myrtle Beach Code Sec. 18-3 (Stormwater, Definitions)
sources.cite: "The equivalent residential unit is 5,000 square feet of impervious surface area." The stormwater chapter's impervious definition is narrower than the zoning code's. North Myrtle Beach Sec. 15-92(c) sets its equivalent runoff unit at 3,500 square feet of impervious area.

sources.label: Fla. Stat. 125.572 — Regulation of synthetic turf
sources.cite: Created by HB 683 (2025), ch. 2025-140. Subsection (3)(a) bars a local government from prohibiting compliant synthetic turf on single-family residential property, or regulating it inconsistently with DEP standards, once DEP adopts rules under the section.

sources.label: Rule 62-308.100, F.A.C. — Synthetic Turf
sources.cite: Effective 19 May 2026, rule file date 29 April 2026, history note "New 5-19-26". This adoption is what triggered the s. 125.572 preemption.

sources.label: Florida DEP proposed rule text for 62-308.100 (January 2026)
sources.cite: "Synthetic turf must be permeable and affixed to permeable backing with a pervious subgrade. A local government may establish a quantifiable standard of a maximum of 10 inches per hour for all layers." Subgrade must be washed natural material; "Soil beneath installed subgrade shall not be compacted to the extent that it adversely impacts percolation"; installations must prevent pooling or an increase in the stormwater runoff volume, direction, or rates to adjacent properties, and may not be installed within a swale, ditch, stormwater pond or a pond's littoral zone. This is the proposed text as published in January 2026, not the adopted rule document.

sources.label: St. Johns County Land Development Code (edition of 4 March 2025)
sources.cite: Article XII: "Impervious Surfaces: Any Building, concrete, pools, wet retention/detention areas, pavement or compacted materials utilized for parking or roadways." Full-text search of the consolidated LDC returns zero occurrences of artificial turf, synthetic turf, artificial grass or synthetic grass.

sources.label: Nassau County Code, Appendix D (Roadway and Drainage Standards), Art. 10 Sec. 10.8(4)
sources.cite: On-site stormwater storage is required for any addition or modification on a developed lot with more than 20 percent impervious area, subject to exemptions including "(c) Pavers are allowed as pervious if shown as engineered with a detail submitted in the application permit" and "(f) Small scale development activities under two-hundred and fifty (250) square feet".

sources.label: Atlantic Beach Code Sec. 24-17 and Sec. 24-89(c)(1)
sources.cite: Impervious surface means surfaces "made of concrete, asphalt, brick, plastic, or any solid surfacing material with a base or lining of an impervious material". Development resulting in more than 35 percent impervious lot coverage must provide on-site stormwater storage for the entire impervious surface area, with a cumulative 400 square foot exemption.

sources.label: St. Augustine Beach Code Sec. 15-17
sources.cite: "Impervious area means any part of any parcel of land that has been modified by the action of persons to reduce the land's natural ability to absorb and hold rainfall... Excluded are all lawns, landscape areas, and gardens or farming areas."

sources.label: City of St. Augustine Code Sec. 29-2 and Sec. 19-16
sources.cite: Sec. 29-2 excludes "all lawns, landscape areas, water and other areas designated by the city manager" from impervious area. Sec. 19-16 lists "artificial turf/sod" among acceptable maintained yard surfaces, expressly contrasted with weeds, gravel and broken concrete.

sources.label: Fernandina Beach Land Development Code Sec. 1.07.00
sources.cite: "Impervious surface means a surface that has been compacted or covered with a layer of material so that it is highly resistant to infiltration by water," including semi-impervious surfaces such as compacted clay. No reference to artificial or synthetic turf appears anywhere in the LDC.

sources.label: Jacksonville Ordinance Code Sec. 654.129
sources.cite: Sets impervious surface ratios by zoning district at subdivision design stage (RR-Acre 30 percent through RHD 85 percent). The Ordinance Code contains no general definition of impervious surface; stormwater facility design is referred out to the Land Development Procedures Manual.

sources.label: HB 803 (2026), ch. 2026-63 — amendment to Fla. Stat. 553.79
sources.cite: "A local government that issues building permits shall exempt an owner of a single-family dwelling or the owner's contractor from the requirement to obtain a building permit to perform any work valued at less than $7,500 on the owner's property." The exemption does not apply to work on property partially or entirely located in a flood hazard area.

sources.label: Colorado HB25-1113 (2025), signed act
sources.cite: Amends C.R.S. Title 37 Article 99 to insert "NONFUNCTIONAL" before "artificial turf" in the prohibition, and adds C.R.S. 37-99-102(6.5) defining functional artificial turf to include playgrounds, sports fields and the playing area of a golf course. Article 99 governs water use; it does not classify turf for stormwater or built-upon-area purposes.

sources.label: Thornton Water — 2026 Artificial Turf Rules for the Water-Wise Landscape Rebate
sources.cite: Requires a minor development permit before installation, backing that drains at a minimum of two inches per hour, a sub-base of at least three inches of compacted aggregate, glued rather than sewn seams, an eight-year fade warranty, and third-party or manufacturer documentation that the product is PFAS-free.
